chunks: From him, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, if a Christian dies and he has a Muslim son, does the Muslim son inherit him?' He said, and he said: 'Yes, indeed God did not increase him by Islam except in honor, so we inherit them and they do not inherit us.'

key_terms.وَلَا يَرِثُونَا: And they do not inherit us

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim son inherit from his Christian father according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Muslim son inherits from his Christian father, affirming the principle that Islam elevates the believer's status, thereby establishing a directional asymmetry in inheritance. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the 'mutual inheritance' (tarath) between Muslims and Ahl al-Kitab, distinguishing it from the general rule where different religions do not inherit from one another. The hadith underscores the theological concept that the spiritual superiority of Islam translates into legal privileges in worldly matters such as inheritance.
